title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is classifying finite maps (cartes) via quotients of the cartographic groups. Here Π_{0,3} is the free group on loops ρ_0, ρ_1, ρ_∞ around 0, 1, ∞ with ρ_0ρ_1ρ_∞ = 1. Π_{0,3}^τ is its semidirect extension by complex conjugation τ, which classifies non-oriented maps. He is giving the topological and algebraic meaning of the generalized triangle groups Π_{0,3}/⟨ρ_i^{ν_i}⟩, with ν_i ∈ N* ∪ {∞}, introduced on the previous page.

(34) Given the signature ν_* = ν_0R_0 + ν_1R_1 + ν_∞R_∞ on P^1_C, he defines X(P^1_C, ν_*). It is the topos of locally separated topological surfaces ramified over P^1_C, with ramification index ν_i over P_i. He first wrote 'dividing' and then crossed it out. The marginal NB says this topos is a topological 'multiplicité', locally a topological surface, and canonically oriented. In modern language it is the 2-dimensional orbifold (topological stack) P^1 with cone points of orders ν_i, i.e. a root stack along the three points. A value ν_i = ∞ means the point is a puncture.

(35) There is a canonical isomorphism Π_{0,3}/⟨ρ_i^{ν_i}⟩ ≅ π_1(P^1(C), ν_*; P_+). By definition this is π_1 of the topos (34) at the base point P_+. This is the standard fact that the orbifold fundamental group of a sphere with three cone points/punctures is the (generalized) triangle group.

(36)-(37) Complex conjugation τ acts naturally on this topos. The 'mixed topos' (the topos with this {1,τ} action, equivalently the quotient stack [X/{1,τ}]) has fundamental group Π^τ_{0,3}/⟨ρ_i^{ν_i}⟩, the extended triangle group. The NB says this is still a topological multiplicité, locally a surface, but no longer orientable. It is the real/Klein orbifold with mirror boundary along RP^1.

(38) Passing to profinite completions gives the étale fundamental group of the algebraic stacky curve (P^1_C, ν_*). This agrees with the one over Q̄ by invariance of π_1^et of proper/tame objects under extension of algebraically closed fields in characteristic 0.

(39) Similarly, the completed extended group is π_1^et of the stack (P^1_R, ν_*). This is an extension of Gal(C/R) = {1,τ} by the geometric group. It is again isomorphic to the group over the real algebraic numbers Q̄∩R.

The page then begins the remark, completed on the next page, that interpretation (38) gives an outer action of Gal(Q̄/Q) on these quotients, and in particular on Π̂_{0,3}. This is the Belyi/Esquisse framework applied to maps with bounded valencies.
errors: Calling X(P^1_C, ν_*) 'the topos des surfaces ... revêtements' is loose. The category of such ramified covers is not itself a topos. What is meant is the classifying topos (orbifold/stack) whose locally constant objects are these covers. The hesitation 'divisant' vs. '=' reflects exactly this: étale objects over the orbifold have ramification dividing ν_i, while the orbifold itself has local index exactly ν_i.

Base point subtlety in (39): for an étale π_1 over R (or Q̄∩R) the base point P_+ must be τ-invariant, e.g. a real (tangential) point or the real segment ]0,1[. If P_+ means the upper half-plane it is not τ-stable. The isomorphism is then only canonical up to inner automorphism or requires a choice. This is not addressed.
Notation drift: the generators are written f_i or ρ_i, and π_{03} vs Π_{0,3}. This is harmless.

ideas.what: Orbifold P^1 with signature ν_* realized as a topos ('multiplicité') whose π_1 is the triangle group Π_{0,3}/⟨ρ_i^{ν_i}⟩
ideas.modern_name: orbifold / root stack fundamental group of a sphere with three cone points; triangle groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thurston (orbifolds, 1978); Fuchsian groups classically (Poincaré, Fricke–Klein); stacky formulation Noohi, Behrend–Noohi (2000s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §3 on cartographic groups and 'multiplicités modulaires'

ideas.what: Complex conjugation acting on the orbifold topos; the 'mixed topos' has π_1 equal to the extended triangle group and is a non-orientable multiplicité
ideas.modern_name: real orbifold / Klein surface orbifold; extended (non-orientable) triangle groups classifying non-oriented maps/hypermaps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jones–Singerman (maps on non-orientable surfaces, 1978); Bryant–Singerman; Köck–Singerman 'real Belyi theory' (2000s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse discusses non-oriented maps and the τ-extended cartographic group; the mixed-topos formulation is not explicit there as far as I know

ideas.what: Profinite completion of the triangle group equals π_1^et of the stacky P^1 over C and over Q̄; the extended version equals π_1^et over R and over Q̄∩R; hence an outer Galois action
ideas.modern_name: étale fundamental group of a stacky curve; Galois action on profinite triangle groups / dessins with bounded valency
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse); Belyi (1979); later Noohi, Zapponi, Köck

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, early (1981) formulation of orbifolds as topoi ('multiplicités'), together with étale π_1 of root stacks over R and Q̄∩R. It is historically nice because it predates the stacky literature. However, the content is the standard triangle-group and dessins picture already announced in the Esquisse and developed later by others.
transcription_corrections: Generators written 'f_i' in the transcription are ρ_i, matching the previous page: Π_{0,3}/⟨(ρ_i^{ν_i})⟩.
'π_{03}' should be Π_{0,3}; in (38) and (39) the groups are the profinite completions Π̂_{0,3} and Π̂^τ_{0,3}.
First marginal NB reads approximately: 'NB ce topos est une multiplicité topologique, loc. surface topologique, elle est canoniquement orientée'.
'Passant aux complétés profinis, on trouve' — the reading is fine; the underbraces under P^1_C and P^1_R say 'schéma'.
Above line (34) there is a crossed-out fragment with '11'. The insertion over 'espaces' is plausibly 'surfaces'.
The last line reads approximately '(et l'interprétation (38) montre qu'il y a une ...', continued on the next page.
